program.name: AI Engineering Lab: a 24-Week AI Engineering Program
program.tagline: Find the Signal. Act with Intelligence.
program.case_study_description: A fictional freight company used as the single running case study across all 24 weeks.

phases.name: Foundations
phases.description: Python, data engineering, classical ML, and deep learning, taught the AI engineering way: every model ships with a metric, a split, and an error analysis.

items.title: Python Foundations & the AI Engineering Landscape
items.objective: Set up a professional AI engineering environment and understand the discipline (Ng's four skills and three loops) while generating the dataset the whole program reuses.
topics: What an AI engineer is: Ng's four skills + three loops
Program map and the ZoroLogistics case study
Git & GitHub workflow (fork, branch, commit, PR)
Python: types, functions, classes, collections, comprehensions
Synthetic data generation with deterministic seeds
items.use_case: Generate the ZoroLogistics synthetic dataset (shipments, carriers, lanes) that every future week reuses.
deliverables: Data dictionary for the generated dataset

checklist.task: Set up VS Code, Python environment (uv or conda), and git; fork/clone the repo.
Complete the Python refresher exercises in the environment notebook.
Run the environment check notebook end-to-end (versions, imports, deterministic seed).
Build the ZoroLogistics data generator: shipments, carriers, lanes, deterministic seeds.
Use case: generate the 100k-row dataset, save to CSV/Parquet, commit it with a data dictionary.
Take the Week 1 quiz (quiz.md), pass with 8/10; record the score in Notes.
Update the Excel tracker: Week 1 checked off; push your fork to GitHub.

items.title: Data Engineering & SQL for AI
items.objective: Clean, profile, and validate real-feeling data with pandas and SQL, and learn the reproducibility habits AI work depends on.
topics: pandas: filter, group, join, pivot, dtypes
Missing data, outliers, and data quality
SQL with DuckDB: joins, aggregations, window functions
items.use_case: Clean and profile the raw shipment dataset into an analytics-ready 'silver' table.
deliverables: SQL analytics queries (on-time rate by carrier/lane/month)

checklist.task: Study data quality concepts; run the pandas refresher exercises.
Run the pandas cleaning notebook; find and document 5 data issues in the generator output.
Write SQL queries in DuckDB: on-time rate by carrier/lane/month, windows, top-lane analysis.
Add a data validation suite (pandera) with at least 10 checks.
Use case: deliver the cleaned silver dataset + profile report; document every cleaning decision.
Take the Week 2 quiz (quiz.md), pass with 8/10; record the score in Notes.
Update the Excel tracker; commit the silver pipeline script.

items.title: Machine Learning Fundamentals
items.objective: Train, evaluate, and compare classical ML models with a rigorous split, metrics, and a first error analysis.
topics: Train/val/test splits, time-aware for freight data
Metrics: MAE, RMSE, accuracy, precision/recall, F1
items.use_case: Baseline ETA (estimated time of arrival) regression and on-time classification from shipment features.
deliverables: ETA regression baseline with logged metrics
On-time classifier with threshold tradeoff analysis
Week 3 model card (metric, split, top error source)

checklist.task: Study supervised learning and the eval mindset: pick the metric before the model.
Run the ETA regression baseline; log MAE/RMSE for 3 models in a comparison table.
Implement a time-aware split and cross-validation; compare models fairly.
On-time classification: precision/recall/F1, threshold tradeoff, confusion matrix.
Use case: write the Week 3 model card (metric, split, top error source) and commit it.
Take the Week 3 quiz (quiz.md), pass with 8/10; record the score in Notes.
Update the Excel tracker; log all experiments to a JSON experiment log.

items.title: Deep Learning with PyTorch
items.objective: Build and train a neural network in PyTorch, tune it with validation, and do the first real error analysis, the habit that defines AI engineering.
topics: Loss functions and optimizers; the training loop
Unpredictable outputs and why DL needs evals + error analysis
items.use_case: A neural ETA model that beats the Week 3 baseline, with a first error analysis by carrier and lane.
deliverables: PyTorch MLP training notebook with learning curves
Neural vs baseline comparison on the test set
Error analysis note: biggest error cluster + hypothesis

checklist.task: Study tensors, autograd, and the computation-graph mental model.
Run the MLP notebook; verify loss curves; deliberately break one thing and diagnose it.
Add dropout/weight decay; tune 3 hyperparameters using the validation split.
Compare neural vs baseline on the test set; segment errors by carrier and lane.
Use case: write the error-analysis note (biggest error cluster + hypothesis).
Take the Week 4 quiz (quiz.md), pass with 8/10; record the score in Notes.
Update the Excel tracker; commit model card v2.

phases.name: LLM Core
phases.description: How LLMs actually work, from tokens and embeddings to attention and the KV cache, then the two engineering superpowers on top: prompt & context-window engineering, and retrieval (RAG + knowledge graphs). Week 8 goes fully local.

items.title: How LLMs Work: Tokens to Transformers
items.objective: Build the correct mental model of what happens between your prompt and the answer: tokenization, embeddings, attention, and generation.
topics: Embeddings: from words to contextual vectors
KV cache and why it matters for cost/latency
items.use_case: Shipment-note token cost estimator plus embedding similarity search over commodity descriptions.

checklist.task: Study tokenization and embeddings (knowledge-base 03).
Tokenizer lab: BPE encode/decode and a token-cost estimator for the LLM API.
Embeddings lab: similarity search over shipment commodity descriptions.
Attention lab: implement scaled dot-product attention in NumPy; visualize the weights.
Use case: build the context-window budget calculator (tokens per call vs window size).
Take the Week 5 quiz (quiz.md), pass with 8/10; record the score in Notes.
Update the Excel tracker; commit both labs.

items.title: Prompt Engineering & the Context Window
items.objective: Engineer prompts and the context around them so a model does a real job reliably, measured by an eval, not by vibes.
topics: Prompt iteration as a measured loop
items.use_case: Extract bill-of-lading fields reliably with a prompt suite and per-field accuracy eval.
deliverables: BoL extraction prompt suite + eval results
Context engineering measurements (tokens, latency, cache hits)

checklist.task: Study prompt engineering and context engineering (knowledge-base 04).
Build the BoL extraction prompt suite; run it against 20 synthetic documents.
Add structured outputs and few-shot examples; improve per-field accuracy.
Context engineering: budgets, compaction, caching. Measure tokens and latency.
Use case: reach 90%+ field accuracy on the eval set; document the failure cases.
Take the Week 6 quiz (quiz.md), pass with 8/10; record the score in Notes.
Update the Excel tracker; commit the prompt suite and eval results.

items.title: RAG, Vector Search & Knowledge Graphs
items.objective: Ground model answers in a corpus (RAG with citations) and in structure (knowledge graphs), and measure retrieval quality.
topics: Vector databases: Chroma, FAISS, pgvector, Weaviate
GraphRAG and when graphs beat vectors
items.use_case: A shipping-policy Q&A bot (RAG with citations) plus a carrier-lane-port knowledge graph.

checklist.task: Study retrieval fundamentals (knowledge-base 05).
Chunk and embed the policy corpus; build a vector index; measure baseline retrieval accuracy.
Add hybrid search and reranking; cite sources in answers; measure groundedness.
Build the carrier-lane-port graph in Neo4j; query shortest and cheapest routes.
Use case: the RAG bot answers 10 unseen questions with citations; log retrieval misses.
Take the Week 7 quiz (quiz.md), pass with 8/10; record the score in Notes.
Update the Excel tracker; commit RAG and graph labs.

items.title: Open Models & Local Inference: GPUs, Ollama, llama.cpp
items.objective: Run open models on your own hardware: pick models by license and VRAM, and operate the local stack (Ollama, llama.cpp, MLX) with confidence.
topics: Open vs closed models; licenses (Apache-2.0, Llama, etc.)
Model families: Llama, Mistral, Qwen, Gemma, DeepSeek, Phi
GGUF format; Ollama, llama.cpp, LM Studio, MLX
GPU setup: CUDA, Apple Metal/MPS, AMD ROCm
Local structured outputs and privacy use cases
items.use_case: Run a local model to triage support tickets offline, plus a VRAM sizing calculator for model choice.

checklist.task: Study the model landscape: open vs closed, licenses, families (knowledge-base 08).
Install Ollama; pull a small model; run chat and structured outputs locally.
Try llama.cpp and MLX; compare tokens/sec across backends in a table.
GPU setup check: CUDA/MPS/ROCm; benchmark with a small script.
Use case: ticket triage with a local model + the VRAM-based model picker.
Take the Week 8 quiz (quiz.md), pass with 8/10; record the score in Notes.
Update the Excel tracker; commit the benchmark table and picker.

phases.name: Model Engineering
phases.description: Make models cheaper and yours: quantization formats and serving engines, fine-tuning with LoRA/SFT/DPO, and the discipline that decides it all, evals and error analysis.

items.title: Quantization & Efficient Inference
items.objective: Shrink models without breaking them, serve them with vLLM, and make quality-vs-cost decisions from data.
topics: Measuring quality loss: perplexity and task evals
items.use_case: Quantize the triage model, serve it with vLLM, and publish a quality-vs-speed report.
deliverables: Quality-vs-cost report with a production recommendation

checklist.task: Study numeric formats and quantization methods (knowledge-base 06).
Quantize a 7B or 8B model with bitsandbytes; measure quality on the triage eval.
GGUF sweep with llama.cpp: Q4/Q5/Q8; record perplexity and speed.
Serve with vLLM (OpenAI-compatible API); benchmark latency and throughput.
Use case: publish the quality-vs-cost report; pick the production quantization.
Take the Week 9 quiz (quiz.md), pass with 8/10; record the score in Notes.
Update the Excel tracker; commit the report.

items.title: Fine-Tuning: LoRA, SFT & DPO
items.objective: Fine-tune small open models efficiently (LoRA/SFT/DPO) and decide, with before/after evals, whether the fine-tune earns deployment.
topics: When to fine-tune vs prompt/RAG (selection order)
SFT dataset formats and chat templates
Fine-tuning on a budget (free Colab tier)
items.use_case: Fine-tune a small open model on ZoroLogistics support tone and bill-of-lading entity extraction.
deliverables: SFT dataset built from the Week 6 corpus
Before/after eval table and a deploy/no-deploy decision

checklist.task: Study fine-tuning theory and the selection order (knowledge-base 06).
Build the SFT dataset (instructions + responses) from the Week 6 corpus.
Train LoRA with TRL/Unsloth (Colab free tier or local GPU); log loss curves.
Create preference pairs; run a small DPO step; compare before/after on the eval.
Use case: publish the before/after eval table; decide deploy vs iterate.
Take the Week 10 quiz (quiz.md), pass with 8/10; record the score in Notes.
Update the Excel tracker; commit the adapter and eval results.

items.title: Evals & Error Analysis for AI Systems
items.objective: Build the reusable eval harness (ZoroEval) that gates every AI artifact in this program, the core AI engineering habit.
topics: Eval design: golden sets and what to measure
Evals in CI; regression suites; drift monitoring
items.use_case: Build ZoroEval, the reusable eval harness that gates every ZoroLogistics AI artifact.
deliverables: Golden eval sets for extraction, RAG, and triage

checklist.task: Study evals and error analysis (knowledge-base 07 + Ng's letters).
Define golden eval sets for extraction, RAG, and triage; implement LLM-as-judge with a rubric.
Run the judges; measure judge agreement; calibrate the rubric.
Error analysis: cluster failures from Weeks 6 to 10 artifacts; pick the top fix.
Use case: ZoroEval v1 gates one artifact in a CI-style script; document the loop.
Take the Week 11 quiz (quiz.md), pass with 8/10; record the score in Notes.
Update the Excel tracker; commit ZoroEval.

phases.name: Harnesses & Loops
phases.description: Become dangerous with coding agents: Claude Code, Cursor, OpenCode, DeepSeek Harness, then run the three loops (agentic coding → developer feedback → external feedback) with a spec, a verifier, and a blast-radius rule.

items.title: Coding-Agent Harnesses: Claude Code, Cursor, OpenCode, DSH
items.objective: Set up and steer the major coding-agent harnesses, and build a real CLI tool with an agent from a spec.
topics: Harness landscape and how to choose
Setup/auth: Claude Code, Cursor, OpenCode, DeepSeek Harness
Managed context: what goes in, what stays out
OpenRouter for model routing; cost control
items.use_case: Build the ZoroLogistics ETA CLI (query tool) entirely with a coding agent from a written spec.
deliverables: ETA CLI built agentically, with tests green

checklist.task: Install and authenticate 2 harnesses (Claude Code + OpenCode or DSH); read the skill guides.
Write SPEC.md for the ETA CLI: user, constraints, one refused tradeoff, test plan.
Drive the agent to build the CLI; run the tests; iterate until green.
Repeat the same task in a second harness; compare plans, cost, and code quality.
Use case: ship the CLI; write the 1-page harness comparison for your team.
Take the Week 12 quiz (quiz.md), pass with 8/10; record the score in Notes.
Update the Excel tracker; commit the CLI and comparison.

items.title: Agentic Coding Loops & Spec-Driven Development
items.objective: Run Ng's three loops on a real MVP: spec → agentic coding with a verifier → developer review → external feedback.
topics: The three loops and their cadences
Verifiers: tests, evals, type checks, linters
Hooks and skills in the harness
Blast-radius rules: production data, secrets, irreversible commands
Measuring the loop: time, tokens, defects
items.use_case: Ship the ZoroLogistics Support Bot MVP through the full three-loop cycle with evals closing every loop.
deliverables: Support bot MVP with a green verifier (unit tests + eval)

checklist.task: Study the three loops and verifier patterns (knowledge-base 01).
Spec the support bot MVP; define the verifier (eval suite + unit tests).
Agentic loop session: build → test → fix until the verifier passes; log the loop.
Developer loop: review with fresh eyes, update the spec, add missed edge cases.
Use case: external loop. Have someone real use the bot; file issues; update spec + evals.
Take the Week 13 quiz (quiz.md), pass with 8/10; record the score in Notes.
Update the Excel tracker; commit the MVP and loop log.

phases.name: Agents
phases.description: From a hand-written ReAct loop to LangGraph state graphs, multi-agent orchestration, and MCP, then OpenClaw as a personal assistant and agent operations.

items.title: Agent Fundamentals: The Loop, Tools & Memory
items.objective: Build an agent from scratch (no framework) so you own the mental model: loop, tools, planning, reflection, guardrails, and traces.
topics: What an agent is; the perceive-plan-act loop
items.use_case: Build the shipment-tracking agent from scratch: lookup, calculator, and web tools.
deliverables: Guardrail tests (refusal, max steps, cost cap)

checklist.task: Study the agent loop and ReAct (knowledge-base 10).
Implement the tool-calling loop by hand; wire 2 tools (track shipment, convert units).
Add planning and reflection; log every step: the trace is your debugger.
Add guardrails: refusal, max steps, cost cap; test adversarial inputs.
Use case: the agent solves 10 unseen scenarios; publish the trace log.
Take the Week 14 quiz (quiz.md), pass with 8/10; record the score in Notes.
Update the Excel tracker; commit the agent and traces.

items.title: Agent Frameworks: LangGraph & the State-Graph Model
items.objective: Move from hand-rolled loops to LangGraph: state, checkpoints, streaming, and human-in-the-loop, and know when a framework earns its complexity.
topics: Why frameworks; the state-graph mental model
LangGraph: nodes, edges, state, conditional routing
Framework comparison: OpenAI Agents SDK, smolagents, Pydantic AI, CrewAI
items.use_case: Re-implement the support agent in LangGraph with a human approval step for refunds.
deliverables: LangGraph support agent with visualized graph

checklist.task: Study graph-based agent design (knowledge-base 10 + LangGraph docs).
Port the Week 14 agent to LangGraph; visualize the graph.
Add checkpoints and resume; crash mid-run and recover.
Add the human-in-the-loop interrupt for refunds over $500.
Use case: end-to-end run with approval; record latency and tokens per node.
Take the Week 15 quiz (quiz.md), pass with 8/10; record the score in Notes.
Update the Excel tracker; commit the graph agent.

items.title: Multi-Agent Systems & MCP
items.objective: Orchestrate a team of agents only where it beats one good agent, measured, and connect everything with MCP.
topics: When multi-agent is worth it (and when it isn't)
MCP architecture: host, client, server; tools/resources/prompts
Evaluating the team vs the single agent
items.use_case: A support triage team: router + specialists (tracking, refunds, docs) over MCP tools.
deliverables: A/B report: multi-agent vs single agent

checklist.task: Study orchestration patterns and MCP (knowledge-base 10/11).
Build an MCP server exposing ZoroLogistics tools; test with an MCP inspector.
Build the multi-agent triage team (supervisor + 3 specialists).
A/B test: multi-agent vs single agent on the same 10 tasks; measure quality and cost.
Use case: publish the A/B report; justify your architecture decision.
Take the Week 16 quiz (quiz.md), pass with 8/10; record the score in Notes.
Update the Excel tracker; commit the team and the MCP server.

items.title: OpenClaw, Hermes & Agent Operations
items.objective: Run OpenClaw as a personal AI assistant with skills and a context loop, drive it with Hermes-class open models, and add the production layer: tracing, evals, and cost.
topics: The OpenClaw context loop and compaction
OpenClaw security model: modes and permissions
Hermes-class open agentic models (Nous Research family)
Running agent brains locally via Ollama
items.use_case: Deploy a personal ZoroLab assistant (OpenClaw) wired to your MCP server, driven by a Hermes-class model.
deliverables: Working OpenClaw installation with 2 custom skills
MCP integration with the Week 16 server

checklist.task: Study OpenClaw and Hermes (reference/agents/ guides + knowledge-base 10).
Install and configure OpenClaw locally; connect a channel (WebChat or Telegram).
Write 2 OpenClaw skills; wire the Week 16 MCP server; test the context loop.
Swap in a Hermes-class model via Ollama; compare assistant quality.
Use case: add tracing and cost tracking to the assistant; publish the ops runbook.
Take the Week 17 quiz (quiz.md), pass with 8/10; record the score in Notes.
Update the Excel tracker; commit skills and the runbook.

phases.name: Cloud AI Platforms
phases.description: The same ZoroLogistics support agent, deployed three ways: Azure AI Foundry (Microsoft), Vertex AI + AI Studio (Google), Bedrock + SageMaker (AWS). Compare capabilities, governance, and cost, then learn how to pick.

items.title: Azure AI Foundry
items.objective: Deploy and evaluate the support agent on Azure AI Foundry: serverless endpoints, agents, evaluation, and AI Gateway governance.
topics: Model catalog and serverless endpoints; Azure OpenAI relationship
AI Gateway (APIM GenAI policies): rate limits, safety
items.use_case: Deploy the support agent to Foundry with online evaluation and gateway rate limits.
deliverables: Foundry agent with tools + evaluation trace

checklist.task: Set up the Azure subscription and AI Foundry hub/project (free tier).
Deploy a serverless model endpoint; call it from the Python SDK and OpenAI SDK.
Create the support agent in Foundry with tools; test in the playground.
Run an online evaluation batch; read the trace; fix the worst failure.
Use case: put the agent behind the AI Gateway (rate limit + content safety); publish cost.
Take the Week 18 quiz (quiz.md), pass with 8/10; record the score in Notes.
Update the Excel tracker; commit the Foundry deployment guide.

items.title: Google Vertex AI & Gemini
items.objective: Use Gemini across AI Studio (fast) and Vertex AI (governed), build a multimodal document pipeline, and evaluate agents on Vertex.
topics: AI Studio (free tier) vs Vertex AI (enterprise)
Model Garden; Agent Builder/Agent Engine + ADK
items.use_case: A multimodal bill-of-lading pipeline: Gemini OCR → structured JSON → BigQuery table.
deliverables: Multimodal OCR notebook with accuracy measurement
Support agent rebuilt with ADK/Agent Engine
End-to-end pipeline with cost per document

checklist.task: Set up Google Cloud and AI Studio; get an API key; check quotas.
Gemini multimodal lab: BoL images → structured JSON; measure accuracy.
Recreate the support agent with ADK/Agent Engine; compare with the Foundry version.
Run a Vertex evaluation on a golden set; log results to BigQuery.
Use case: end-to-end pipeline (images → clean table); publish cost per document.
Take the Week 19 quiz (quiz.md), pass with 8/10; record the score in Notes.
Update the Excel tracker; commit the Vertex guide.

items.title: AWS Bedrock & SageMaker AI
items.objective: Build on Bedrock (Converse API, Knowledge Bases, Agents, Guardrails) and SageMaker AI, then finish the three-cloud comparison.
topics: Bedrock Converse API and model catalog (Claude, Nova, Llama, Mistral)
Bedrock Agents; Guardrails; Prompt Management; AgentCore
SageMaker AI: training, JumpStart, HyperPod, Model Customization, serving
Pricing: on-demand vs provisioned throughput, cross-region inference
items.use_case: A Bedrock RAG support agent with Guardrails, plus the Great Platform Comparison matrix.
deliverables: Converse API prompt-suite run across Bedrock models
Bedrock Agent + Guardrails; three-cloud comparison matrix

checklist.task: Set up the AWS account and IAM least-privilege role; enable Bedrock models.
Converse API lab: run the Week 6 prompt suite across Bedrock models.
Build a Knowledge Base (RAG) for shipping policies; query with citations.
Create a Bedrock Agent + Guardrails; test blocked prompts.
Use case: publish the 3-cloud comparison matrix (Foundry vs Vertex vs Bedrock) with cost.
Take the Week 20 quiz (quiz.md), pass with 8/10; record the score in Notes.
Update the Excel tracker; commit the AWS guide and matrix.

phases.name: Databricks Zero to Hero
phases.description: The full Zorost Databricks modernization playbook: Unity Catalog, Delta Lake medallion, DBSQL, PySpark, streaming, Lakeflow, MLflow, Mosaic AI, Genie, then DABs, CI/CD, governance, and FinOps, ending in the lakehouse capstone.

items.title: Databricks Day Zero: Unity Catalog & the Lakehouse
items.objective: Stand up a governed lakehouse: Unity Catalog, Delta Lake, DBSQL, and the medallion architecture in pure SQL.
topics: The Data Intelligence Platform and workspace anatomy
Unity Catalog: metastore, catalogs, schemas, volumes, tables
Delta Lake: ACID, time travel, VACUUM, OPTIMIZE, liquid clustering
Medallion architecture in SQL (bronze → silver → gold)
items.use_case: Stand up the ZoroLogistics lakehouse: bronze → silver → gold entirely in SQL.
deliverables: Silver/gold medallion tables + first AI/BI dashboard

checklist.task: Create the Databricks account/workspace (free trial); tour the UI.
Unity Catalog lab: create catalog/schema/volume; load CSV data; grant rights.
Delta Lake lab: create tables, time travel, VACUUM, OPTIMIZE, liquid clustering.
Medallion in SQL: bronze raw → silver clean → gold aggregates for shipments.
Use case: governed silver/gold tables with lineage; build a first AI/BI dashboard.
Take the Week 21 quiz (quiz.md), pass with 8/10; record the score in Notes.
Update the Excel tracker; commit the SQL notebooks.

items.title: Databricks Data Engineering: PySpark, Streaming & Lakeflow
items.objective: Engineer data at scale with PySpark, streaming, and declarative Lakeflow Pipelines, with data quality expectations and scheduled Jobs.
topics: Lakeflow Pipelines (formerly Delta Live Tables): streaming tables, materialized views, expectations
items.use_case: A streaming pipeline: live shipment events → validated silver → on-time KPIs.
deliverables: DLT pipeline with expectations (data quality gates)

checklist.task: PySpark lab: transform shipment data with DataFrames; compare with SQL.
Write a DLT pipeline in Python (or SQL) with expectations on data quality.
Add a streaming table for live shipment events (Auto Loader/streaming source).
Create a Lakeflow Job: schedule and orchestrate the pipeline; check runs and lineage.

Take the Week 22 quiz (quiz.md), pass with 8/10; record the score in Notes.
Update the Excel tracker; commit the pipeline code.

items.title: Databricks ML & GenAI: Training, Serving, Genie
items.objective: Run the full Mosaic AI stack: MLflow, point-in-time feature engineering, model serving, Vector Search, AI functions, and Genie.
topics: MLflow experiments and the model registry
UC feature engineering: feature tables, FeatureLookup, point-in-time joins
Training: scikit-learn/XGBoost/PyTorch, AutoML, Databricks Model Training
Model Serving endpoints + Unity AI Gateway
AI Search (Vector Search) and RAG on Databricks
AI functions: ai_query, ai_classify, ai_extract, ai_gen…
Genie Agents; Agent Bricks and Agent Evaluation
items.use_case: A point-in-time ETA model + RAG over shipping docs + a Genie space for ops analysts.
deliverables: Registered ETA model with point-in-time features
Serving endpoint behind the AI Gateway
Vector Search RAG + Genie space with verified answers

checklist.task: MLflow + feature tables: log a baseline; build point-in-time features.
Train the ETA model (XGBoost or PyTorch); register it in MLflow; compare challenger.
Create the serving endpoint + AI Gateway rate limit; call from Python.
Vector Search: index policy docs; build the RAG chain with ai_query.

Take the Week 23 quiz (quiz.md), pass with 8/10; record the score in Notes.
Update the Excel tracker; commit the ML assets.

items.title: Databricks Production: DABs, Governance & the Capstone
items.objective: Ship everything as code: Asset Bundles, CI/CD, governance, FinOps, then deploy the full ZoroLogistics Lakehouse Intelligence capstone.
topics: Databricks Asset Bundles (databricks.yml): jobs, pipelines, dashboards as code
Git folders and CI/CD for bundles
Governance: row filters, column masks, dynamic views, lineage, system tables
FinOps: billing tables and cost dashboards
Certification paths (Data Engineer, Data Analyst, ML, GenAI Engineer)
